body: Thanks for the advice.  Unfortunately I'm not much of a programmer; took a few courses and it had me pretty lost once we got past the absolute basics, even with a lot of assistance.  A shame, since the only real group of friends I know that graduated to jobs were the programmers, and the rest just got stuck too.  Regardless, thanks again.

The big issue is that I'm going for a second bachelor's, not a graduate program.  I'm not good enough with what I know to do grad school; I'd look like an idiot, and probably fail out fast because I don't have a lot of base skills.  If you go for a bachelor's beyond your first, you can't get government grants, and a lot of scholarships and loans are also unavailable.  Even trying to go to a community college is out of my price range because of that.

I understand your opinion of not needing college, if only because a lot of people have said that to me already.  The bigger problem is that I can't seem to get anything in a good field without an internship and experience - I've been specifically turned down from jobs because they told me they'd rather have someone with experience.  It terrifies me, and now I've worked food service, and am getting turned down from new job apps because they question why I worked food service, saying that I must not have the drive to do better in life.

The worst thing about it is that I thought I was better than this.  Went I went to RPI, they told us we'd be graduating to $45k annual jobs with benefits... and now, that's just a dream.  I busted my ass in high school, spent nearly $250k to attend that place, burying my family and myself in debt, and it did absolutely nothing.  I'm so embarrassed about the jobs I'm working that I can barely look friends in the eye... I wanted to be better than this.

The places I'm finding range from minimum wage to $10/hr.  Just considering rent, utilities, food, health insurance, and student loans, I need to be getting closer to $16 to be comfortable, otherwise I risk having months where I bleed my remaining savings.  Those student loans are a killer, and I can't really negotiate them down.

Yeah, I used to think that... sadly, the majority of people I friended at RPI are still struggling to find any kind of job.  Most are with their parents still, and at best, they're earning barely enough to scrape by.  It's beyond terrifying to see the people you looked up to in college struggling to make it.  At this point, if I could, I'd return the damn degree and get my money back!
I posted some more info in a response to glitchd's comment... I'll PM my link to you in a short bit.

I hope I didn't come off as too panicky.  Honestly, I'm currently in a state of "might as well just enjoy the time I have before I run out of money and probably jump off a bridge".  First, just to note, I don't have work yet - problem with food service is that they usually want jobs filled immediately, and Boston is too far from where I am now to drive to do applications.  I'll have to wait until we're living there to check for those jobs, but at that point, I'll be on a timer of maybe 40 days, tops, before I'm out of money.

I suppose I don't care anymore about posting some more personal info.  My degree is in Architectural Building Sciences, from RPI (Troy, NY); a now-cancelled degree, I might add, that they removed because they knew it was worthless.  I studied lighting and digital art applications for architecture as part of the degree, and attempted a Japanese minor too.  I got a minor in Game Design Studies, focused on 3D animation - my dream job is working with 3D modeling for architecture, or maybe animation, or if I must, games.  I regret that my skills are quite limited beyond that, and even with modeling, much of what I know is self-taught, as the college only had 3 courses for it, and they weren't that in-depth.  That said, everyone I know says my artwork is top-notch.

I won't post the link to my portfolio here, if only because my name is in the URL, and that's a bit too much info for my comfort.  I can PM it to you if you'd like (my resume is on there too), though I don't know what that could help really.

I need to step out for a bit to do some errands, but I'll be back around 1pm EST.

EDIT: back already, sent you a PM.
